package.title: TensorSPH 3-D operators: what the analytic benchmarks actually verify (mission m5054)
package.repro_cmd: python3 -m ke.sediment_extract --spec knowledge/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054/spec.json --source-repo /root/tensor-ecosystem/TensorSPH --out knowledge/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054 --run-dir docs/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054/runs/extract && python3 -m ke.sediment_verify --package knowledge/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054 --spec knowledge/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054/spec.json --source-repo /root/tensor-ecosystem/TensorSPH --run-dir docs/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054/runs/extract --report docs/sediment/tk-sediment-m5054/runs/validate/validate_report.json

activity.description: Spec-driven extraction of the 3-D SPH operator verification delivered by mission m5054: every quote is located programmatically in the pinned blobs of TensorSPH@82b72a15, every reference value in the benchmark table is recomputed from the committed report JSON with the formula stored beside it (2*nu*k^2 for the unsteady-Stokes decay rate, rho0*g*(H-dx/2) for the hydrostatic bottom pressure, the analytic kernel normalisation integrals). Producer writes draft/unassessed records only; independent review is not performed here.

claims.statement: At TensorSPH@82b72a15 the 3-D cubic-spline kernel satisfies both normalisation identities to double precision on the source lattice: sum(W*dV) = 1 with error 4.0e-15 and sum(r^2*laplacian(W)*dV) = 6 with error -1.5e-10; the discrete Laplacian at the origin equals the analytic value digit for digit. Residual error in the 3-D operators therefore cannot be blamed on the kernel.

conditions: lattice quadrature with h = 0.013, dx = h/1.3
exclusions: does not cover boundary truncation of the kernel support
does not cover the 2-D kernel (10/(7 pi h^2) normalisation)

notes: The two identities are the standard admissibility conditions for an SPH kernel (Monaghan 1992).
Values are the committed artifact's, re-derived by the benchmark table (rows kernel-integral, kernel-second-moment, kernel-laplacian-origin).

claims.statement: The lattice mass-calibration constant C is identical to all digits on every resolution of the dx ladder (dx = 0.02 -> 0.0025, spread exactly 0.0), and at h/dx = 1 the residual mass bias is -2.75e-5 on the tension side, where the Tait equation clamps it to p = 0. The bias is therefore a property of the lattice geometry, not a discretisation error that shrinks with dx: one calibration per lattice suffices.

scope.system: tensorsph.threed lattice calibration + Tait equation of state
exclusions: does not cover disordered particle packing

notes: Practical consequence: resolution studies must not re-tune C, or the ladder measures the calibration, not the scheme.

claims.statement: On the operator ladder the second-moment-renormalised Laplacian is monotone in kh (relative L2 error 19.37 % -> 11.36 % -> 5.20 % -> 2.96 % for kh = 0.681, 0.511, 0.340, 0.255) while the raw Laplacian is not (5.38 % -> 4.01 % -> 11.24 % -> 13.87 %): the raw operator is twice as accurate at kh = 0.681 and only the renormalised one converges. Renormalisation is thus a fine-kh measure (kh <~ 0.34 on this lattice), not a blanket improvement.

scope.system: symmetric pressure force + second-moment-renormalised viscous Laplacian on a periodic cubic lattice
exclusions: does not test wall-bounded or free-surface truncation

notes: Belytschko/Randles corrected-SPH literature predicts convergence, not coarse-grid superiority; the coarse-grid crossover is the part worth remembering.
The source's own criterion only asks for < 5 % at the finest grid, so a reader of criteria alone would miss the crossover.

claims.statement: The 3-D unsteady-Stokes shear benchmark reports verdict 'fail' although all six of its criteria are true: the failure is missing case h1.8 in missing_cases. Its headline number (decay-rate error within 2.7 %) holds only on the finest rung (n = 24, -2.68 %); n = 12 is -12.62 %, and at n = 20 the unrenormalised operator is +11.46 % while the renormalised one is -4.18 %. Any citation of the 2.7 % figure must carry kh and the operator variant.

scope.system: 3-D double-shear (unsteady Stokes) on a triply periodic cube, nu = 0.05, k = 2*pi, amplitude 0.1, c0 = 10 m/s
exclusions: does not cover free-surface or wall-bounded shear

notes: verdict 'fail' + all criteria true is the artifact's structural signature: verdict folds in coverage (missing cases), criteria fold in physics. Both must be read.

claims.statement: The hydrostatic-column benchmark reports verdict 'fail' with 4 of 8 criteria false. Its 2.75 % bottom-pressure error exists only for the best run (Adami wall, c0 = 20): c0 = 10 gives -4.30 %, c0 = 5 gives -8.74 %, the Tait-only wall model gives -25.23 %, and the per-layer core maximum relative error is 43.17 %. The 2.7 % figure is therefore a single bottom-load number and must not be read as per-layer pressure accuracy.

scope.domain: SPH hydrostatic pressure / wall boundary condition
scope.system: 3-D wall-bounded column at rest, 8x8 base, nz in {12,16,24}, rho0 = 1000 kg/m^3, g = 9.81 m/s^2
exclusions: does not cover dynamic free-surface cases

notes: The failed criteria are interior_pressure_within_15pct_best, bottom_pressure_within_15pct_all, column_settled_window_drift_below_2pct and centre_of_mass_drift_below_1pct.
Re-derived reference: p_bottom = rho0*g*(H - dx/2) = 1000*9.81*0.155 = 1520.55 Pa.

claims.statement: Mission m5054 is an honest partial delivery, not a closed one: at its pinned commit the README advertises the 3 %-level 3-D verification and links docs/verification_threed.md, but that file does not exist at 82b72a15 (git cat-file -e exits 128), and the committed guard test tests/test_threed_artifacts.py asserts verdict == 'pass' for the shear and hydrostatic reports while both committed reports say 'fail'. Executing that guard file against the pinned artifacts gives 2 failed / 1 passed (runs/m5054/source_guard/source_guard.json). Operator core is verified; documentation and the artifact/guard contract are not.

scope.system: TensorSPH 3-D branch (tensorsph.threed) as delivered by mission m5054
exclusions: does not assert that the physics tests fail; the operator tests pass at the pin

notes: This is the recomputed counterpart of the mission's own honest-FAIL statement, so the negative result is registered rather than overwritten.
Reproduction: see runs/m5054/source_guard/repro.sh and the run JSON.

benchmarks.name: tensorsph-threed-operator-benchmarks
benchmarks.description: Every reference value below is recomputed by ke.sediment_extract from the pinned report JSON: exact kernel normalisation integrals, the analytic Laplace symbol -9*(1/(pi h^3))/h^2, the unsteady-Stokes decay rate 2*nu*(2*pi/L)^2, the hydrostatic bottom load rho0*g*(H-dx/2). 'got' is the committed artifact number. Rows outside tolerance are kept, not dropped.

rows.ref_label: rho0*g*(H - dx/2), Tait-only wall model (control run)
continuum second moment K = 2 (lattice value may differ)

external_anchors.label: Monaghan 1992, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics, Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys. 30:543-574
external_anchors.why: defines the kernel admissibility conditions (unity and second-moment normalisation) used by claims kernel-quadrature-exact and mass-calibration-lattice-constant

external_anchors.label: Morris, Fox & Zhu 1997, Modeling low Reynolds number incompressible flows using SPH, J. Comput. Phys. 136:214-263
external_anchors.why: source of the renormalised viscous operator family against which laplacian-renorm-scope is judged

external_anchors.label: Randles & Libersky 1996, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics: some recent improvements and applications, CMAME 139:375-408
external_anchors.why: corrected-SPH / reproducing-condition lineage behind the second-moment normalisation

external_anchors.label: Adami, Hu & Adams 2012, A generalized wall boundary condition for smoothed particle hydrodynamics, J. Comput. Phys. 231:7057-7075
external_anchors.why: defines the wall model whose hydrostatic bottom load is the headline of hydrostatic-headline-is-a-single-point

external_anchors.label: Colagrossi & Landrini 2003, Numerical simulation of interfacial flows by smoothed particle hydrodynamics, J. Comput. Phys. 191:448-475
external_anchors.why: documents the spurious pressure / odd-even mode at free surfaces that the hydrostatic per-layer table exposes
